package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affected Mac and Windows versions distributed prior to March 30th, 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CX Desktop App was compromised via a software supply chain attack, resulting in the distribution of malicious code within trusted application binaries. The attackers inserted malware into the app, which was then delivered to end users through official update mechanisms, enabling targeted information theft.

execution_context.file_location: Electron app binary (possibly within a third-party dependency or a bundled resource file)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code hidden within an 'icon' file downloaded from a GitHub repository named 'IconStorages'. The file, while appearing to be a benign image or icon, actually contains executable malware that is loaded and run by the compromised 3CX app.
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely shellcode or compiled binary, possibly loaded via JavaScript or native code in Electron)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the application downloads a file from a GitHub repository ('IconStorages'), interprets it as an icon, but actually loads and executes embedded malware code, which then performs information theft and exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The application downloads and executes code from an external, non-official source (GitHub) at runtime, using a file that masquerades as a benign icon but contains malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Electron apps should not download and execute code from untrusted sources, especially not from public GitHub repositories under the guise of image assets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may download icons or images for UI updates, but should never execute code from such files.
key_indicators: Download of executable content disguised as an image/icon
Execution of code from a file fetched at runtime from a public repository
Use of a benign-sounding repository name ('IconStorages') to evade detection

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the 3CX app or one of its dependencies during the build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of compromised app to end users

attack_chain.action: End users install or update the 3CX app, receiving the compromised binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code on user systems

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the compromised app downloads a file from the 'IconStorages' GitHub repository, treating it as an icon but actually loading and executing embedded malware.
The malware performs information theft (e.g., targeting cryptocurrency companies) and exfiltrates data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration and potential further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Electron app downloading files from public GitHub repositories at runtime
Execution of code from files masquerading as images or icons
Unexpected network requests to GitHub or other non-official sources after app launch
file_indicators: Files downloaded from 'IconStorages' or similarly named repositories
Icon or image files with unexpected executable content
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure for data exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Electron-based applications for runtime downloads of files from public repositories, especially when such files are used as icons or images but contain executable content. Flag any execution of code from non-official, externally downloaded resources. Correlate network activity to known attacker infrastructure and unusual GitHub repository access.
